«Switching a session's model and effort — a verb with no side effect on the user's settings; the console reaches it
through «Console actions» (v2-31)». No freight block stands on it (`pins`: none for `chk-ke32dhty`), no carry, no
`BLOCKED-ON`.

- A viola verb that switches a running viola-wrapped session (a named instance) to a given model and effort, and
  records the new pair so that a later resume (`revive`, `up`) replays the NEW pair, not the one named at launch.

- The verb has no side effect on the user's own settings: it writes nothing to `~/.claude*` or to a project's
  `.claude/settings*`, and does not use the CLI's own model command as its channel (v2-31's requirement: «the CLI's
  model command writes the user-scope model key, so it is not the channel»).

- Its argument surface, closed words, exit codes, hints, output lines, `--json` document, the events-log record of the
  switch, and its process-log lines, each beside the existing tables (architecture's CLI verbs, exit-cause catalogue,
  obs-plan's closed details, events.md's kinds).
- Out: the console's keyboard reach of the switch — «Console actions» (v2-31's console clause) owns it.
- Out: the real CLI observed running on the pair — carried to «The fleet on the founder's host» (`cry-s4qhj2e3`).
- Out unless a fork settles otherwise: an MCP tool for the switch (the directive's conservative arm is CLI-only).

- Nothing live in this phase: no live start, no window, no key, no real session read, switched, ended or resumed, no
  read of the operator's real `~/.claude*`, no `viola list` against the real board (the directive, cited below).

- v2-31 «Switch a session's model and effort» — its acceptance names two legs: the switch taking effect for the next
  turn with the user's settings byte-identical, and the console reaching it by keyboard alone. The console leg is
  «Console actions»'s, so whether this chunk can claim v2-31 is P4's lean on the cap's requirement and the route's
  lines naming it `[inferred]`.

- v2-30 «Model and effort named at launch» — unclaimed; its `open`, `up` and `adopt` clauses now have their verbs
  (`up` and `adopt` gated on R4 and R5). Whether this chunk can claim it, and on what, is read at P4 `[inferred]`.

- `[inferred]` `viola revive` already takes `--model` / `--effort`, which override the recorded pair on the resumed
  child's argv (`src/cmd/revive.rs`, `given_pair`); a start appends one `launch {model, effort}` line, and the
  snapshot holds `launch` (`viola_state::snapshot::Launch`). So a restart-based switch could ride the existing start
  path, and the record a resume replays may already be the last `launch` line.

- `[inferred]` The ways a running session's model or effort can change are: a restart through `revive` with a new
  pair (it ends and resumes the session); a command typed into the live session; a settings write. Which of these

body:
- **M1 — the ways a running session's model or effort can change, as viola's code and ledger hold them:**
  - (a) a restart that resumes the session with a new pair. `viola revive <name> --model M --effort E` hands each given half over the recorded one (`src/cmd/revive.rs:278-298`, `given_pair`; witnessed by `tests/cli_revive.rs:878`, `revive_hands_the_recorded_pair`). It runs only on a GONE instance: a live holder of the name is refused by `run`'s collision check (`src/cmd/revive.rs:233`), and a session a live claude holds is refused `session-live` (`src/cmd/revive.rs:244`). The resume itself rests on the relied ledger row `resume-session` — «--resume <id> reopens the session under that id» (`crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger.rs:156`, predicate `session_resumed` at `:1546`: the resumed SessionStart has source `resume` and the same `session_id`). Writes: viola's own events log and snapshot only.
  - (b) a command typed into the live session. The ledger's `LOCAL_COMMANDS` holds 7 names — `/clear` · `/remote-control` · `/compact` · `/mcp` · `/cost` · `/usage` · `/context` (`crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger.rs:236-244`) — and no `/model` or `/effort`. No `LedgerRow` names a model or effort command (the row names and their claims, `ledger.rs:117-170`, read whole; the predicate match `:1628-1690`). What such a command writes, and whether a typed one is confirmed by viola's send, is UNMEASURED by the ledger. The only statement that it writes the user-scope model key is the cap's own requirement text (`cap:viola-0.2.0/v2-31`, «the operator's ruling 2026-11-09»), not a recorded row.
  - (c) a settings write. viola writes no Claude settings at any start: «A start hands its child no --settings and writes no settings.json in the instance directory; the user's settings are left byte- and mtime-equal» (`test-plan · contract/viola-run-start/settings`), and no ledger row records what a settings write would change. UNMEASURED.

- **M2 — what `revive` does today with the recorded pair:** each half is the `--model` / `--effort` given, else the recorded half while it still parses (`is_model_word` / `is_effort_level`), else the start's default (`src/cmd/revive.rs:278-298`; `architecture · decision/revive-pair-from-record`). A given pair overrides the recorded one: yes.

- **M3 — where the pair is recorded and what a switch must append:** every start appends one `launch {model, effort}` events line (`source: wrapper`, after `lineage`) and holds the pair in the snapshot's `launch` (`architecture · contract/event-data/launch`, `contract/instance-snapshot/launch`); a replay takes the LAST `launch` line (`crates/viola-state/src/replay.rs:125`, `apply_launch_line`). A later `launch` line also clears the replayed window record: `crates/viola-state/src/replay.rs:145` (`Some(EventKind::Launch) => *window = None`). So a switch that appends a `launch` line makes a later resume replay the NEW pair, and on a replayed snapshot it drops the window record unless a `window` line follows it.

- **M4 — the closed sets and where they are checked:** model words `viola_core::is_model_word` (`crates/viola-core/src/lib.rs:411-418`: 1–64 bytes, a lower-case letter first, then lower-case letters, digits, `.`, `-`) — a shape, not a list; efforts `viola_agent_claude::EFFORT_LEVELS` = `low · medium · high · xhigh · max` (`crates/viola-agent-claude/src/lib.rs:166`, `is_effort_level` `:173`); clap value parsers `parse_model` / `parse_effort` (`src/cmd/run.rs:87`, `:95`); the compiled default `DEFAULT_PAIR = ("opus", "medium")` (`lib.rs:170`); a configured default from `config.json` `default_model` / `default_effort` (`src/run/launch.rs:18-19`).

- **M5 — what a switch of a session mid-turn or holding a dialog meets:** the wrapper holds the running-turn state (`src/run/wheel.rs:182`, `turn_running`), the wheel holder and human typing (`wheel.rs:113`, `:119`) and the one pending dialog slot (`src/run/dialog.rs`). `send` refuses `not-delivered` / `turn-running` while a turn runs (`src/run/send.rs:126`, `:156`). No code path ends a running session child today: the product kills a PTY child only on a worker panic (`crates/viola-pty/src/pump.rs:381`, `kill_and_reap`) and in verify's own probe runs; the PTY seam's `kill` reaches portable-pty 0.9.0's child kill, which sends SIGHUP first (`portable-pty-0.9.0/src/lib.rs:344-347`). What the real CLI does on that signal mid-turn, mid-dialog or idle (whether its transcript is whole for the resume) is UNMEASURED.

- **M6 — whether the switch can be read back:** no. «Every start, run, revive and adopt, hands the claude child a model and effort pair on its command line; the pair is never read back or verified» (`architecture · decision/launch-pair-handed-not-verified`). The recorded 2.1.328 SessionStart payloads carry a `model` key only on a `compact` start (`fixtures/claude/2.1.328/SessionStart.compact-1.json`; the `resume-1`, `clear-1` and `default` payloads hold none — key names read by a one-line JSON key listing over each file). So «takes effect for its next turn» is not observable from the fakes or the hooks: it rests on the real CLI, carried to «The fleet on the founder's host» (`cry-s4qhj2e3`).
- `src/run/launch.rs` (full) — the pair's resolution: given half wins, missing half from `config.json`, else `DEFAULT_PAIR`; `names_pair` refuses a pair after `--`
- `src/cmd/revive.rs` (1-300) — the preflight order (holder → session → live elsewhere → recorded dir), `given_pair`, the `Launch` it hands `run::start`

- `src/cmd/run.rs` (223-282, 766-850) — the channel dispatch (`dispatch_call`: `send · wait · last · hook.dialog · answer · pause · release · link · unlink`), `Launch`, `spawn_child`, `pump_child` (the wrapper ends when the child exits)
- `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/lib.rs` (150-190) — `resume_args`, `MODEL_FLAG`, `EFFORT_FLAG`, `EFFORT_LEVELS`, `DEFAULT_PAIR`, `launch_args`
- `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger.rs` (225-265, 1546-1553, 1628-1690) — `LOCAL_COMMANDS`, the relied rows, `session_resumed`
- `crates/viola-core/src/lib.rs` (411-418) — `is_model_word`
- `crates/viola-state/src/replay.rs` (125-150) — the last `launch` line wins; a `launch` line clears the replayed window
- `src/run/wheel.rs` (110-250) — turn, wheel and typing state the wrapper holds
- `src/run/send.rs` (120-160) — the turn-running refusal
- `crates/viola-pty/src/lib.rs`, `crates/viola-pty/src/pump.rs` (function list) — `Pty::kill`, `pump_with_paste`, `PumpEnd`, `kill_and_reap`
- `fixtures/claude/2.1.328/SessionStart.*.json` (key names only) — which starts report a model
- `tests/cli_revive.rs` (857-900) — `revive_hands_the_recorded_pair`, the witness for M2

- derived-without-graph — the plan's mechanism is still a fork (§Open questions); the caller sets of `pump_child`, `run::start` and the dispatch table are taken from the graph at P4 once the mechanism is chosen, never from memory.

- **A start is the one path to a child** (`src/cmd/run.rs:378`, `start`; revive and adopt build a `Launch` and call it): a new child with a new pair is a start, and every start writes `wheel`, `lineage`, `launch` (and under `--origin` `window`) lines.
- **Wrapper-served methods refuse in closed words before acting** (`src/run/send.rs:126-156`): the send path reads human-typing and turn-running before anything is issued, under the one flight lock.

body:
_Generated by /andromeda-phase P4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not
edit during an /implement run._
- **Marker:** 2026-11-24-switching-a-session-s-model-and-effort · **Version:** viola-0.2.0

A new CLI verb, `viola switch <name> [--model <MODEL>] [--effort <EFFORT>] [--json]`, switches a RUNNING wrapped
session to a given model and effort. It does this by an in-place restart served by the session's own wrapper.

- **The wrapper's side:** a new channel method `switch` reads the session idle and the human off the keys. The wrapper
  then ends its OWN claude child, appends one `launch {model, effort}` line, and respawns `claude --resume <the
  session's id>` with the new pair in the same PTY, directory and terminal. The window, socket, wheel holder, links
  and lineage stay.

- **The record:** the new `launch` line is the last one, so a later `viola revive` or `viola up` replays the NEW pair
  (`architecture · decision/revive-pair-from-record`, research M2–M3).

- **The user's settings:** nothing is written to the user's Claude settings or config. The switch does not pass
  through `run::start`, so it makes no trust-record write and no automatic verify. It types nothing into the session
  (research M1).

The mechanism is founder fork F1, taken on its arm 1 and PROVISIONAL: a new channel method, and a wrapper ending its
own live child, are boundary widenings (`security-plan · decision/new-listener-needs-log-entry`;
`.andromeda/runs/2026-11-24T12-23-47Z-phase/founder-forks.md`, Block 1). Two more of his forks are taken on their
conservative arms meanwhile:
- F3: a switch is REFUSED mid-turn, with a dialog pending or while the human types.
- F5: the verb is CLI-only, with no MCP tool.

The technical proposals F2, F4 and F6 stand until the overseer's relay. The real CLI running on the new pair is never
read back (`architecture · decision/launch-pair-handed-not-verified`, research M6); that reading is carried to «The
fleet on the founder's host» (`cry-s4qhj2e3`). This chunk claims no capability (P4 lean, Provenance).

1. **The pump outlives one child** (`crates/viola-pty/src/pump.rs`, `crates/viola-pty/src/lib.rs`).
   - **The request:** add a respawn request handle beside `PasteHandle`, given to `pump_with_paste` as one more
     argument. A request carries a `SpawnSpec` and a reply slot.
   - **On a request, in order:**
     - the pump ends the current child through `Pty::kill`, which portable-pty 0.9.0 sends as SIGHUP first (research
       M5);
     - it reaps the child within the compiled bound `RESPAWN_REAP_BOUND` (10 s, F6);
     - it spawns the request's `SpawnSpec` through `spawn`, and swaps the new PTY under the same host stdin and stdout
       copies;
     - it answers the reply slot with `Respawned { exit, child_pid }`.
   - **If the reap passes its bound:** the old child is left running, nothing is spawned, and the slot reads
     `NotEnded`.
   - **If the spawn fails:** the slot reads `SpawnFailed`. The pump then ends as on a child exit, returning
     `PumpEnd::Exited` with the old child's exit.
   - `pump_with_paste` returns only when a child exits with no request standing.
   - The seam knows no agent and takes no viola crate (`architecture · decision/pty-knows-no-agent`).
   - Keeps tests S2–S4 and S6 (inline `#[cfg(test)]` cases, rstest tables, literal oracles, the `Pty` seam's own
     doubles).

2. **The wrapper's `switch` method** (new `src/run/switch.rs`, registered in `src/run/mod.rs`, routed in
   `src/cmd/run.rs` `dispatch_call`).
   - **Params:** `{v, sender, model?, effort?}`. It reads no `from`.
   - **Param checks:** each given half is re-checked by `viola_core::is_model_word` /
     `viola_agent_claude::is_effort_level`. Neither given, a half of another type, or a half failing its check is
     `-32602` with `data: null`, and nothing is written.
   - **Refusals, under the one wrapper flight lock (`architecture · decision/send-flight-lock`), first one wins:**
     1. `human-typing`;
     2. `not-delivered` / `turn-running`;
     3. `not-delivered` / `dialog-pending`, a new detail word;
     4. `unverified-cli` (the CLI's stamp does not count `resume-session`, or the snapshot reads `cli_verified:false`);
     5. `not-delivered` / `no-session` (the snapshot's `agent_session_id` is absent or fails `is_session_id`).
   - **The pair:** each half given, else the wrapper's own recorded `launch` half.
   - **Once the refusals pass, in order:**
     1. build the child's `SpawnSpec` with `crate::run::child_launch` (the plugin-dir flag, `launch_args(model,
        effort)`, then `viola_agent_claude::resume_args(id, false)` as the user words), the start's program, recorded
        cwd and strip plan;
     2. send the respawn request;
     3. on `Respawned`: append the `launch` line, then, where the snapshot holds a window record, its `window` line
        again;
     4. update the snapshot's `launch` and `child_pid`;
     5. answer `{"ok":{"model","effort"}}`.
   - **The `launch` order:** the line is appended inside the pump's sequence, AFTER the old child's reap and BEFORE
     the spawn. This is a callback the request carries, run between the two, so a wrapper killed after the reap
     leaves the new pair recorded (founder-forks Block 1, directive item 6).
   - **The other outcomes:**
     - `NotEnded` → refusal `not-delivered` / `child-not-ended`, nothing appended;
     - `SpawnFailed` → refusal `not-delivered` / `resume-failed`, the wrapper then ending (the `launch` line already
       stands, so `viola revive` resumes on the new pair).
   - **The wheel:** the holder is unchanged and no `wheel` line is written.
   - **Logs:** the method writes the channel pair only, plus the existing `log_child_exit` / `log_child_start` pair
     for the two children, with no pair, model or session id in any line
     (`security-plan · decision/launch-pair-kept-to-snapshot-and-event-log`).

3. **The verb** (new `src/cmd/switch.rs`, dispatched in `src/cmd/mod.rs`).
   - **Arguments:** `<name>` through `parse_name`; `--model` / `--effort` through `run::parse_model` /
     `run::parse_effort`, a clap group requiring at least one (exit 2); `--json`.
   - **Order:** `client::refuse_untrusted` (exit 21, no line), then `live_endpoint`, then `client::connect` (the
     socket-dir check, the peer euid and the server check), then ONE `switch` frame.
   - **Reading the reply:** through `reply_of`, every refusal mapped to its existing exit: 10 human-typing,
     12 unverified-cli, 13 not-delivered, 14 unknown, 20 wrapper fault, 21 unreachable.
   - **Output:** the human line is `<name>  switched  <model> <effort>` on stdout. Under `--json`:
     `{"v":1,"ok":{"model":…,"effort":…}}` or the refusal document.
   - **Logs:** as `cli` into `cli-<name>.ndjson` inside the dispatch span `cli.switch`, after the instance check.
   - Keeps security S-lines for frame verbs (`security-plan · decision/cli-frame-verbs-strict-modes-first`,
     `decision/client-seam-check-order`).

4. **Help and words.**
   - `src/cmd/mod.rs`'s help rows: `setup:` becomes `open, run, revive, adopt, up, switch, verify, plugin install`.
   - Hints in `src/human/hints.rs` for `dialog-pending`, `no-session`, `child-not-ended` and `resume-failed` (none
     names `viola release`).
   - The `HELP` literal in `tests/cli_output_plain.rs`.

5. **The closed tables.**
   - The new error bodies' writers in `tests/contract_error_bodies.rs`.
   - Each new cause in `tests/cross_exit_causes.rs`.
   - The new closed detail words in `schemas/diag-line.v1.json`, each entering with its emitter.

7. **Integration cases** (new `tests/cli_switch.rs`, every case named `switch_…`, over `booted_wrapper` /
   `stamped_home`, the fake agent on a test-scoped PATH, under a test-owned user home).
   - `switch_of_an_idle_session_resumes_it_on_the_new_pair`:
     - one new `launch` line read from the switch's own offset;
     - the new child's argv read from `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` carries `--resume <id> --model M --effort E`
       (`test-plan · decision/child-argv-read-from-proc`);
     - one `session-start` of cause `resume` with the same id;
     - the wrapper's pid unchanged;
     - exit 0 and the human line.
   - `switch_keeps_the_user_settings_byte_and_mtime_equal`: the test-owned HOME's `.claude.json` and `.claude/`
     files are byte- and mtime-equal before and after (`test-plan · contract/viola-run-start/settings`).
   - `switch_then_revive_replays_the_switched_pair`: the wrapper ended by its tie, then `viola revive` without a pair,
     whose `launch` line carries the switched pair.
   - `switch_mid_turn_is_refused_turn_running`: exit 13; no `launch` line.
   - `switch_with_a_dialog_pending_is_refused_dialog_pending`: exit 13; no `launch` line.
   - `switch_while_the_human_types_is_refused_human_typing`: exit 10.
   - `switch_with_neither_flag_is_usage`: exit 2.
   - `switch_with_a_bad_effort_is_usage`: exit 2.
   - `switch_of_a_gone_instance_is_instance_dead`: exit 21, `--json` detail `instance-dead`.
   - `switch_json_prints_the_pair_document`.
   - Keeps tests S1 and S3–S7: own home, waits on events with no sleep, literal oracles, synthetic inputs with the
     canary, real stubs, tied spawns that drop `VIOLA_*`.

1. **The pump outlives one child** (`crates/viola-pty/src/pump.rs`, `crates/viola-pty/src/lib.rs`).
   - **The request:** add a respawn request handle beside `PasteHandle`, given to `pump_with_paste` as one more
     argument. A request carries a `SpawnSpec` and a reply slot.
   - **On a request, in order:**
     - the pump ends the current child through `Pty::kill`, which portable-pty 0.9.0 sends as SIGHUP first (research
       M5);
     - it reaps the child within the compiled bound `RESPAWN_REAP_BOUND` (10 s, F6);
     - it spawns the request's `SpawnSpec` through `spawn`, and swaps the new PTY under the same host stdin and stdout
       copies;
     - it answers the reply slot with `Respawned { exit, child_pid }`.
   - **If the reap passes its bound:** the old child is left running, nothing is spawned, and the slot reads
     `NotEnded`.
   - **If the spawn fails:** the slot reads `SpawnFailed`. The pump then ends as on a child exit, returning
     `PumpEnd::Exited` with the old child's exit.
   - `pump_with_paste` returns only when a child exits with no request standing.
   - **What the pump owns across a respawn:**
     - It owns the respawned child: the caller's `&mut dyn Pty` is the FIRST child only, and the `PumpEnd` exit is the
       LAST child's.
     - The host-input copy thread and the job queue (`HumanInput`, the `PasteHandle`'s sender) persist across a respawn.
     - The writer thread and the output copy thread are ended for the old child (`end_writer`'s bound, `KILL_WAIT`)
       and started again on the new child's writer and reader.
     - The panic arm (`kill_and_reap`, `pump.rs:381`) kills the CURRENT child.
     - A host size change is applied to the new child, which is spawned at the current host size.
   - `pump()` (`pump.rs:293`) and verify's typed run (`src/cmd/verify/typed/run.rs:152`) pass a respawn handle no one
     requests on, so their behaviour is unchanged.
   - The seam knows no agent and takes no viola crate (`architecture · decision/pty-knows-no-agent`).
   - Keeps tests S2–S4 and S6 (inline `#[cfg(test)]` cases, rstest tables, literal oracles, the `Pty` seam's own
     doubles).

2. **The wrapper's `switch` method** (new `src/run/switch.rs`, registered in `src/run/mod.rs`, routed in
   `src/cmd/run.rs` `dispatch_call`).
   - **Params:** `{v, sender, model?, effort?}`. It reads no `from`.
   - **Param checks:** each given half is re-checked by `viola_core::is_model_word` /
     `viola_agent_claude::is_effort_level`. Neither given, a half of another type, or a half failing its check is
     `-32602` with `data: null`, and nothing is written.
   - **Refusals, under the one wrapper flight lock (`architecture · decision/send-flight-lock`), first one wins:**
     1. `human-typing`;
     2. `not-delivered` / `turn-running`;
     3. `not-delivered` / `dialog-pending`, a new detail word;
     4. `unverified-cli` (the CLI's stamp does not count `resume-session`, or the snapshot reads `cli_verified:false`);
     5. `not-delivered` / `no-session` (the snapshot's `agent_session_id` is absent or fails `is_session_id`).
   - **The pair:** each half given, else the wrapper's own recorded `launch` half.
   - **Once the refusals pass, in order:**
     1. build the child's `SpawnSpec` with `crate::run::child_launch` (the plugin-dir flag, `launch_args(model,
        effort)`, then `viola_agent_claude::resume_args(id, false)` as the user words), the start's program, recorded
        cwd and strip plan;
     2. send the respawn request;
     3. on `Respawned`: append the `launch` line, then, where the snapshot holds a window record, its `window` line
        again;
     4. update the snapshot's `launch` and `child_pid`;
     5. answer `{"ok":{"model","effort"}}`.
   - **The `launch` order:** the line is appended inside the pump's sequence, AFTER the old child's reap and BEFORE
     the spawn. This is a callback the request carries, run between the two, so a wrapper killed after the reap
     leaves the new pair recorded (founder-forks Block 1, directive item 6).
   - **The other outcomes:**
     - `NotEnded` → refusal `not-delivered` / `child-not-ended`, nothing appended;
     - `SpawnFailed` → refusal `not-delivered` / `resume-failed`, the wrapper then ending (the `launch` line already
       stands, so `viola revive` resumes on the new pair).
   - **The wheel:** the holder is unchanged and no `wheel` line is written. At the respawn the wrapper clears the
     held scheduled-wakes count (`count_wakes(None)`), as a `session-start` does (`src/run/send/slot.rs:263-266`).
   - **A late hook of the old child:** from the respawn request until the new child's `session-start` arrives, the
     wrapper holds a switch mark. Once that `session-start` has arrived, a `session-end` carrying the switched
     session's id is not appended while the new child's pid is alive: the old child's SessionEnd hook can reach the
     wrapper after the new child starts, and both carry one session id. A `session-end` arriving BEFORE the new
     `session-start` is appended as any is: the log records the old process ending.
   - **Logs:** the method writes the channel pair only, plus the existing `log_child_exit` / `log_child_start` pair
     for the two children, with no pair, model or session id in any line
